sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Jackson County?
sections.html:
Property tax in Jackson County, Illinois runs through three courthouse-area offices in Murphysboro. The Treasurer collects, in the courthouse at 1001 Walnut Street, open Monday through Friday until 4 in the afternoon, phone 618-687-7350. The Chief County Assessment Officer's staff and the Board of Review sit at 900 Walnut Street, at 618-687-7220 and 618-687-7226.

The treasurer's page is blunt about what that office cannot do: it has no authority to set the amount of a bill, change it or alter a mailing address.

  • Questions about an assessment: the township assessor or the Chief County Assessment Officer.
  • Missing exemptions and address changes: the assessment office.
  • Appeals of value: the Board of Review.
  • Prior-year back taxes that were sold: the County Clerk at 618-687-7360.

The county's Property Tax Lookup lets you search any parcel and print a bill, which is handy when a bill never arrived. Under state law the tax stays owed even if a bill is not received.

sections.h2: What is Jackson County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Jackson County sits in the Little Egypt region of southern Illinois, about 98 miles southeast of St. Louis. It was organized on January 10, 1816, with Brownsville as its first seat, and Murphysboro took over after the courthouse burned in 1843. Carbondale is the largest city and the home of the main campus of Southern Illinois University. The land area is about 584 square miles. Murphysboro, Carbondale, Ava and Grand Tower are the cities, and the March 18, 1925 Tri-State Tornado struck Murphysboro, Gorham and De Soto hard.

QuickFacts from the Census Bureau puts the county at 52,501 people in July 2025, compared with 52,974 counted in 2020, and 27,715 housing units.

  • Owners live in 50.0 percent of occupied homes, so renters make up the other half.
  • A typical home lived in by its owner is valued at $137,300 for 2020 to 2024, while median gross rent is $782.
  • Median household income is $48,763, and 20.5 percent of residents live in poverty.
  • Four building permits were issued in 2025, and 36.3 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree or higher.

Owners of rental houses should ask the assessment office what class and exemptions the parcel record shows before listing.

sections.h2: What dates did the 2026 Jackson County tax calendar set?
sections.html:
The treasurer's calendar for 2025 taxes payable in 2026 set the first installment at September 4, 2026 and the second at November 4, 2026. Payments in any amount are accepted up to January 21, and an installment paid after its due date carries a 1 1/2 percent penalty for each month or part of a month.

After the sale date, late taxes are paid at the County Clerk's Office. Mobile home bills are due each year on July 1, and the state-mandated late penalty is $25 per month up to a maximum of $100.

sections.h2: How can I pay a Jackson County tax bill?
sections.html:
The county accepts online, phone, mail, bank and in-person payments. Online card or e-check payments go through Municipay, and the phone line for card payments is 618-492-4566. A secure drop box sits at the top of the accessible ramp at the Chestnut Street entrance to the courthouse, and checks or certified funds only go in it.

  • By mail: Jackson County Treasurer, P.O. Box 430, Murphysboro, IL 62966-0430.
  • At a bank: most Jackson County banks take payments on or before each installment date, but they will not take mobile home payments.
  • Fees: 2.5 percent with a $2.00 minimum for credit or debit cards, and $1 for e-checks.
  • Prepaying: the treasurer lets you make estimated monthly payments toward the next bill free of interest.

The Property Tax Inquiry page gives your parcel number (PIN), or you can call the treasurer's office to get it.

sections.h2: Where does Jackson County property tax money go?
sections.html:
The county's explanatory page shows how a recent tax year (2024 taxes payable 2025) was split among the districts. Schools take most of it.

  • All schools: 63.69 percent.
  • County purposes: 19.01 percent.
  • Cities, villages and incorporated towns: 7.37 percent.
  • Townships and road districts: 4.75 percent, and park districts 2.39 percent.
  • Airport, fire protection, conservancy, library and other districts share the remaining fraction.

The assessed value is 33 1/3 percent of fair market value, excluding farmland and farm buildings. The 2025 assessment notice put the required level at 33.33 percent and the countywide median level at 29.08 percent, with Carbondale at 30.85 percent, Murphysboro at 29.86 percent and Makanda at 26.50 percent. A district's own levy and your exemptions then drive the dollar amount, which is why two houses with similar values can get different bills.

sections.h2: What is the process for contesting a Jackson County assessment?
sections.html:
An appeal must be filed with the Board of Review inside 30 days of the date the Supervisor of Assessments publishes the township's values. For 2026 the publication was set for October 29 and the deadline for the end of day on November 30, 2026. That window has closed, and the board's FAQ says no extensions are possible.

The board reviews value only. A bill that seems too high, a percentage jump or a neighbor's lower bill is not by itself a ground. Overvaluation, equity, physical data errors and preferential assessment are the four recognized reasons.

  • File one form per parcel, with evidence such as a recent appraisal, a settlement statement from the last two years or a comparison grid.
  • Only the owner or an attorney may file, and partnerships, LLCs and corporations need an Illinois attorney.
  • Hearings are generally held by teleconference or phone, and failing to attend can get an appeal dismissed.
  • If you reject the proposed decision, you have 10 days to request a hearing, then 30 days from the final decision to go to the Property Tax Appeal Board.

If a hearing falls after a due date, the county advises paying the amount due and waiting for a refund. A taxpayer who objects after those steps pays under protest and files a tax objection complaint with the Circuit Clerk. A certificate of error can fix factual mistakes such as wrong square footage, but only for the current bill and before the annual tax sale.

sections.h2: What happens when Jackson County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
The county mails a certified letter, publishes the unpaid parcel in a newspaper, and then offers the tax at the annual sale. Buyers bid an interest rate between 0 and 9 percent. The sale auctions the unpaid tax, not the house.

The county's explanation says that if the owner does not redeem for 30 months, the tax buyer can ask the court for a tax deed. Statute section 21-350 now sets 3 years for certificates issued on or after January 1, 2024, so ask the County Clerk which period applies to your parcel. If no buyer bids, the tax goes to the Jackson County Trustee, and a deed the Trustee obtains goes to an annual sealed bid auction where the buyer is not responsible for the back taxes. The treasurer's page notes the last day to bid on the 2025 surplus auction was November 15, 2025.

Redemption of prior-year taxes is handled by the County Clerk at 618-687-7360.

sections.h2: What should I settle before selling a house in Jackson County?
sections.html:
Work through a short checklist before you accept an offer.

  • Print the parcel's tax history from the lookup page and check which installments were paid.
  • Ask the treasurer for a payoff when a penalty is accruing or a tax sale date is near.
  • Ask the assessment office how to remove your owner-occupied exemption once you move.
  • Ask the Board of Review whether an appeal on the parcel is still pending.
  • Photograph repairs that a buyer may price in.

A cash buyer can take a Jackson County house in as-is condition, and any tax balance is paid from the funds at closing.

faqs.q: When are Jackson County property taxes due?
faqs.a: For 2025 taxes payable 2026, the treasurer listed September 4 and November 4, 2026. A 1 1/2 percent penalty applies for each month or part of a month after an installment date.

faqs.q: Where is the Jackson County Treasurer's office?
faqs.a: It is in the Jackson County Courthouse at 1001 Walnut Street in Murphysboro, open 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday through Friday. The phone number is 618-687-7350.

faqs.q: What was the 2026 assessment appeal deadline in Jackson County?
faqs.a: The Board of Review set publication for October 29, 2026 and the deadline for the end of day on November 30, 2026. That deadline has passed, and the board does not grant extensions.

faqs.q: How do I pay Jackson County taxes online?
faqs.a: Use the Municipay link on the treasurer's page. Cards carry a 2.5 percent fee with a $2.00 minimum, and e-checks carry a $1 fee.

faqs.q: Who handles back taxes sold at a Jackson County tax sale?
faqs.a: The County Clerk, at 618-687-7360. Ask for the redemption amount and deadline on the specific parcel.
